title: The Works of Philo Judaeus
authorityNotice: Ancient Jewish philosophical and biblical interpretation. It is included for historical study and is not presented as Scripture.
collectionNotice: This collection follows the forty-five-work C. D. Yonge contents list. Appendix materials and fragmentary works are identified in their titles.

works.title: On the Creation
works.estimatedDate: Probably c. 20–40 CE; exact date uncertain
works.purpose: To explain Genesis 1 as a philosophically ordered account of creation and to present Moses as a wise lawgiver whose law accords with the structure of the cosmos.

works.title: Allegorical Interpretation, I
works.estimatedDate: First half of the first century CE; exact date uncertain
works.purpose: To interpret the early chapters of Genesis allegorically as teachings about the soul, reason, sensation, virtue, and humanity’s relationship with God.

works.title: Allegorical Interpretation, II
works.estimatedDate: First half of the first century CE; exact date uncertain
works.purpose: To continue Philo’s allegorical reading of Genesis, using Adam, Eve, Eden, and related figures to examine the movements and failures of the human soul.

works.title: Allegorical Interpretation, III
works.estimatedDate: First half of the first century CE; exact date uncertain
works.purpose: To extend the allegorical interpretation of Genesis by contrasting virtue and passion and explaining biblical characters and actions as realities within the soul.

works.title: On the Cherubim
works.estimatedDate: First half of the first century CE; exact date uncertain
works.purpose: To interpret the cherubim, the flaming sword, Cain, and related Genesis passages as symbols of divine powers, human desire, and the soul’s moral choices.

works.title: On the Birth of Abel and the Sacrifices Offered by Him and by His Brother Cain
works.estimatedDate: First half of the first century CE; exact date uncertain
works.purpose: To contrast Abel and Cain as patterns of God-centered and self-centered life and to explain what makes worship and sacrifice acceptable.

works.title: That the Worse is Wont to Attack the Better
works.estimatedDate: First half of the first century CE; exact date uncertain
works.purpose: To use Cain’s attack on Abel as an allegory of vice opposing virtue and to encourage the soul’s resistance to passion and false reasoning.

works.title: On the Posterity of Cain and His Exile
works.estimatedDate: First half of the first century CE; exact date uncertain
works.purpose: To interpret Cain’s descendants and exile as a spiritual history of self-love, pleasure, violence, and alienation from God.

works.title: On the Giants
works.estimatedDate: First half of the first century CE; exact date uncertain
works.purpose: To interpret Genesis 6 and the giants as an account of souls drawn toward bodily passion rather than heaven, virtue, and the Spirit of God.

works.title: On the Unchangableness of God
works.estimatedDate: First half of the first century CE; exact date uncertain
works.purpose: To defend God’s unchanging nature while explaining biblical language about divine grief, anger, and judgment in ways consistent with divine perfection.

works.title: On Husbandry
works.estimatedDate: First half of the first century CE; exact date uncertain
works.purpose: To use biblical farming imagery to distinguish the wise cultivation of the soul from destructive self-indulgence and false education.

works.title: Concerning Noah's Work as a Planter
works.estimatedDate: First half of the first century CE; exact date uncertain
works.purpose: To interpret Noah as a planter of virtue and to explore how education, cultivation, and disciplined practice shape the soul.

works.title: On Drunkenness
works.estimatedDate: First half of the first century CE; exact date uncertain
works.purpose: To examine literal and figurative drunkenness as loss of reason, while contrasting intoxication by passion with sober wisdom and divine inspiration.

works.title: On the Prayers and Curses Uttered by Noah When He Became Sober
works.estimatedDate: First half of the first century CE; exact date uncertain
works.purpose: To interpret Noah’s words after becoming sober and explain the moral and symbolic significance of blessing, servitude, family, and self-mastery.

works.title: On the Confusion of Tongues
works.estimatedDate: First half of the first century CE; exact date uncertain
works.purpose: To interpret Babel and the confusion of languages as a judgment on arrogance and as an allegory of disordered passions, speech, and thought.

works.title: On the Migration of Abraham
works.estimatedDate: First half of the first century CE; exact date uncertain
works.purpose: To portray Abraham’s migration as the soul’s departure from bodily attachments and merely human reasoning toward God, wisdom, and virtue.

works.title: Who is the Heir of Divine Things?
works.estimatedDate: First half of the first century CE; exact date uncertain
works.purpose: To explain what it means to inherit divine things through Abraham’s story, emphasizing faith, spiritual perception, virtue, and God’s gifts.

works.title: On Mating with the Preliminary Studies
works.estimatedDate: First half of the first century CE; exact date uncertain
works.purpose: To use Abraham, Sarah, and Hagar to explain how preliminary education can serve wisdom without replacing the higher pursuit of virtue.

works.title: On Flight and Finding
works.estimatedDate: First half of the first century CE; exact date uncertain
works.purpose: To interpret biblical stories of fleeing and finding as movements of the soul away from passion and toward refuge, discipline, self-knowledge, and God.

works.title: On the Change of Names
works.estimatedDate: First half of the first century CE; exact date uncertain
works.purpose: To explain the changes of biblical names as signs of transformed character, deeper perception, and progress from created things toward knowledge of God.

works.title: On Dreams, That They are God-Sent
works.estimatedDate: First half of the first century CE; exact date uncertain
works.purpose: To classify and interpret biblical dreams, distinguishing divine revelation from dreams arising through the soul, imagination, or confused passion.

works.title: On Abraham
works.estimatedDate: Probably c. 20–40 CE; exact date uncertain
works.purpose: To present Abraham’s life as an unwritten embodiment of natural law and as a model of faith, hospitality, virtue, and devotion to the one God.

works.title: On Joseph
works.estimatedDate: Probably c. 20–40 CE; exact date uncertain
works.purpose: To present Joseph as a statesman and political administrator, examining prudence, self-control, governance, and life amid the complexities of public power.

works.title: On the Life of Moses, I
works.estimatedDate: Probably c. 20–40 CE; exact date uncertain
works.purpose: To present Moses to non-Jewish and Jewish readers as an exemplary king and lawgiver whose life reveals wisdom, courage, justice, and divine calling.

works.title: On the Life of Moses, II
works.estimatedDate: Probably c. 20–40 CE; exact date uncertain
works.purpose: To continue the portrait of Moses as lawgiver, priest, and prophet and to explain the character, purpose, and sacred authority of his work.

works.title: The Decalogue
works.estimatedDate: Probably c. 20–40 CE; exact date uncertain
works.purpose: To explain the Ten Commandments as universal headings of the Mosaic law and to show their order, ethical reach, and grounding in devotion to God.

works.title: The Special Laws, I
works.estimatedDate: Probably c. 20–40 CE; exact date uncertain
works.purpose: To organize laws associated with the first commandments, explaining priesthood, worship, sacrifice, holiness, and devotion to the one God.

works.title: The Special Laws, II
works.estimatedDate: Probably c. 20–40 CE; exact date uncertain
works.purpose: To organize and interpret laws concerning worship, festivals, vows, social duties, and the practical formation of a just and grateful community.

works.title: The Special Laws, III
works.estimatedDate: Probably c. 20–40 CE; exact date uncertain
works.purpose: To explain laws governing marriage, sexual conduct, family relationships, and justice, relating particular commands to broader moral principles.

works.title: The Special Laws, IV
works.estimatedDate: Probably c. 20–40 CE; exact date uncertain
works.purpose: To explain laws concerning property, testimony, appetite, justice, and social responsibility as applications of the Decalogue’s general principles.

works.title: On the Virtues
works.estimatedDate: Probably c. 20–40 CE; exact date uncertain
works.purpose: To gather Mosaic teachings and narratives around courage, humanity, repentance, and nobility, presenting virtue as the lived purpose of the law.

works.title: On Rewards and Punishments
works.estimatedDate: Probably c. 20–40 CE; exact date uncertain
works.purpose: To conclude the exposition of the law by describing the blessings of obedience, the consequences of rebellion, and the possibility of repentance and restoration.

works.title: Every Good Man is Free
works.estimatedDate: Probably an early work, within the first half of the first century CE
works.purpose: To argue in Stoic terms that the truly virtuous person is inwardly free even under outward oppression, while the person ruled by passion is a slave.

works.title: On the Contemplative Life or Suppliants
works.estimatedDate: First half of the first century CE; exact date and relationship to Philo’s other works are uncertain
works.purpose: To describe the Therapeutae and their disciplined communal life of prayer, study, simplicity, worship, and contemplation as an example of devotion.

works.title: On the Eternity of the World
works.estimatedDate: Date uncertain; attribution to Philo has been disputed
works.purpose: To survey and assess philosophical arguments about whether the cosmos is created, destructible, or eternal; the surviving work may not preserve its original conclusion.

works.title: Flaccus
works.estimatedDate: After 41 CE, probably in the early 40s CE
works.purpose: To recount the persecution of Alexandria’s Jewish community under the prefect Flaccus, condemn his abuses, and interpret his downfall as divine justice.

works.title: Hypothetica: Apology for the Jews
works.estimatedDate: First half of the first century CE; exact date uncertain; survives only in fragments
works.purpose: To defend Jewish origins, laws, communal discipline, and moral practice for a wider Greco-Roman audience.

works.title: On Providence: Fragment I
works.estimatedDate: Date uncertain; preserved fragmentarily and with textual complications
works.purpose: To defend divine providence against objections raised by suffering, disorder, and apparent injustice in the world.

works.title: On Providence: Fragment II
works.estimatedDate: Date uncertain; preserved fragmentarily and with textual complications
works.purpose: To continue the defense of divine providence by considering the ordered cosmos, moral government, and the place of apparent evil.

works.title: On the Embassy to Gaius: The First Part of the Treatise on Virtues
works.estimatedDate: After 41 CE, probably in the early 40s CE
works.purpose: To record the Alexandrian Jewish embassy to Emperor Gaius, expose the danger of imperial claims to divinity, and defend Jewish loyalty to God and ancestral law.

works.title: Questions and Answers on Genesis, I
works.estimatedDate: First half of the first century CE; exact date uncertain; surviving transmission is incomplete
works.purpose: To answer interpretive questions arising from Genesis by combining literal explanation, allegory, philosophy, and moral instruction.

works.title: Questions and Answers on Genesis, II
works.estimatedDate: First half of the first century CE; exact date uncertain; surviving transmission is incomplete
works.purpose: To continue a question-and-answer interpretation of Genesis, explaining difficult details through literal, symbolic, philosophical, and ethical readings.

works.title: Questions and Answers on Genesis, III
works.estimatedDate: First half of the first century CE; exact date uncertain; surviving transmission is fragmentary
works.purpose: To preserve further answers to interpretive problems in Genesis, especially through allegorical and philosophical exposition.

works.title: Appendix 1: Concerning the World
works.estimatedDate: Date and authorship uncertain; included in older collections of Philonic writings
works.purpose: To discuss the world’s creation, structure, order, and relation to its Creator in a philosophical-theological framework.

works.title: Appendix 2: Fragments
works.estimatedDate: Various dates; fragmentary material attributed to Philo with differing degrees of confidence
works.purpose: To preserve otherwise lost portions and testimonies associated with Philonic interpretation, philosophy, and Jewish apologetic thought.
